\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{A Spectral Remedy Frontier for Coordinated Polymer Repair}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We convert the link-lift obstruction into an exact quantitative target for a coordinated multi-star repair.\end{abstract}
Let $\lambda$ bound external curvature energy relative to the repaired centered mode, let $a$ be the contraction, and let $D_0=m\eta^2$. Including fixed losses $J$, define
\[F(\eta,a,\lambda)={(1-a^2)D_0\over2t}-{(1-a)^2\lambda D_0\over2t}-c(m-1)\log(1/a)-J.\]
\begin{theorem}A coordinated repair closes the channel whenever
\[\lambda<{(1-a^2)-{2t\over D_0}(c(m-1)\log(1/a)+J+F_*)\over(1-a)^2}.
\]
The inequality includes action, spillover, Jacobian, Haar, comparison, and target free energy.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Subtract the minimum external action increase from the selected-star action drop, then apply the change-of-variables determinant and the declared fixed losses. Solving $F>F_*$ for $\lambda$ gives the criterion.\end{proof}
Across the complete nonlinear split interval, the measured single-star spill coefficient fails. At the upper split it must be reduced to the calibrated admissible fraction recorded by the executable frontier.
\begin{remark}This is a noncircular design target. It does not construct the coordinated gauge-covariant repair.\end{remark}\end{document}
